title: 7 Reasons Creatine Is Worth a Look After 40
meta_description: What research says about creatine after 40: muscle creatine stores, lean mass and strength with resistance training, and why daily consistency matters.

hero.title: Creatine Is Worth a Look After 40

items.title: A well-studied ingredient
items.body:
The International Society of Sports Nutrition reviewed creatine monohydrate research and found that it raises muscle creatine stores and can support high-intensity exercise and lean mass gains during training.

That review also described creatine as generally well tolerated in healthy people. Have a medical condition or take medication? Ask your clinician first.
items.alt: Hex dumbbells, a steel water bottle and a folded towel on a bright home gym mat

items.title: It tops up muscle stores
items.body:
In a classic study of 31 men, muscle creatine rose about 20% after a high-dose loading week.

A lower daily amount reached a similar rise more gradually, over 28 days. The study measured muscle creatine, not strength.

chart.title: Muscle creatine relative to baseline
chart.source: Hultman et al., J Appl Physiol 1996. 31 men; muscle creatine rose about 20% after six days or 28 days, depending on the approach.

items.title: Training still does the work
items.body:
In a meta-analysis of older adults, creatine paired with resistance training produced greater chest-press and leg-press strength gains than training alone.

The pattern matters: creatine was studied as a training partner, not as a substitute for lifting.
items.evidence: Meta-analysis, Open Access J Sports Med 2017
items.alt: An older adult's hands holding a dumbbell beside a gym bench, with no face visible

items.title: Lean mass rose with lifting
items.body:
The same meta-analysis found more lean tissue mass when creatine was added to resistance training.

Its participants were older adults, and the result came from structured training studies. It does not mean the supplement replaces progressive exercise.

chart.title: Creatine plus resistance training
chart.source: Chilibeck et al., Open Access J Sports Med 2017. 22 randomized trials, 721 participants; lean tissue mass difference 1.37 kg.

items.title: Loading is optional
items.body:
Loading fills muscle stores faster, but a steady daily routine reaches a similar level more gradually, according to the evidence review.

That gives you a choice of pace. The research does not make a loading phase a requirement.
items.evidence: Evidence review, J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2021
items.alt: A scoop beside a shaker bottle and a clean kitchen sink, with no product packaging visible

items.title: Consistency keeps stores up
items.body:
In the 1996 study, muscle creatine stayed elevated while participants continued the routine.

After they stopped, levels moved back toward baseline in about 30 days. The practical lesson is less about a perfect start and more about a habit you can repeat.
items.alt: A weekly planner, glass of water and dumbbell on a calm kitchen counter

items.title: The format can help
items.body:
The studies above used repeated routines, not occasional use. A supplement only fits the evidence if the habit fits your real week.

That makes convenience a practical question, not a performance claim: will you remember it on training days and rest days alike?
items.evidence: Study-design pattern across the cited sources
items.alt: A gym bag, water bottle and bright green FusiForce pouch on a linen bench

bridge.title: Convenience is part of consistency
bridge.body:
The research used a daily routine. The practical question is which routine you will actually remember.

Powder can mean measuring, mixing and cleaning up. Those small steps may become friction when you are rushing out the door or packing for a trip.

If format is the obstacle, FusiForce is one option: creatine monohydrate in a chewable gummy, with Green Apple or Blueberry flavor.
